cluster_genes.affinage_functional_annotation: AAMP is a WD40- and immunoglobulin-domain-containing protein that promotes cell migration and angiogenesis by acting as a signaling scaffold for Rho-family GTPases. AAMP stabilizes RhoA by binding it and suppressing SMURF2-mediated ubiquitination and degradation, thereby sustaining RhoA/Rho kinase signaling downstream of VEGF to drive actin stress fiber formation and endothelial tube formation [PMID:26350504, PMID:34901393]. AAMP also activates CDC42 by displacing its GAP (ARHGAP1), promoting cellular protrusions and invasion [PMID:33279622], and binds Nod2 through its WD40 domains to modulate NF-κB-mediated innate immune signaling [PMID:19535145]. AAMP turnover is itself regulated by ubiquitination, and its levels control endothelial barrier integrity and the stability of both RhoA and RhoB [PMID:39404373].

BMS1 is an essential nucleolar GTPase that functions as a GTP-regulated molecular switch within the SSU processome (90S pre-ribosome) to drive 18S rRNA maturation and 40S ribosomal subunit biogenesis. GTP binding to BMS1 is thermodynamically coupled to recruitment of RCL1 and U3 snoRNA into a stable ribonucleoprotein subcomplex; RCL1 in turn acts as a guanine-nucleotide exchange activator for BMS1, while the BMS1 C-terminal domain functions as an intramolecular GAP [PMID:16307926, PMID:16376378]. BMS1 also interacts with the replication-fork barrier protein Ttf1 and uses its GTPase activity to dissociate the Ttf1–RFB complex, thereby coordinating rDNA transcription with replication during S-phase [PMID:34791311]. A heterozygous missense mutation (p.R930H) in BMS1 causes autosomal dominant aplasia cutis congenita through impaired 18S rRNA processing and a p21-mediated G1/S cell-cycle delay [PMID:23785305].

BOP1 is a nucleolar WD40 repeat protein that serves as the central scaffold of the trimeric PeBoW complex (with Pes1 and WDR12), essential for processing of 32S pre-rRNA into mature 28S and 5.8S rRNAs and biogenesis of 60S ribosomal subunits [PMID:10891491, PMID:15225545, PMID:16043514]. BOP1 depletion or dominant-negative disruption triggers nucleolar stress that activates p53 through RPL11-mediated inhibition of MDM2, enforcing G1 cell cycle arrest independently of p19ARF [PMID:11390653, PMID:16043514, PMID:33510838, PMID:38409361]. Beyond ribosome biogenesis, BOP1 overexpression promotes epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition through RhoA activation, drives chromosomal instability via Aurora kinase B phosphorylation, and enhances Wnt/β-catenin signaling by recruiting CBP to acetylate β-catenin, thereby supporting cancer stem cell properties [PMID:21520196, PMID:32805281, PMID:33797754]. BOP1 protein stability is regulated by direct binding of lncRNAs CCAT2 and SNHG6, and BOP1 loss modulates MAPK signaling by downregulating DUSP4/DUSP6 phosphatases, conferring resistance to BRAF inhibitors in melanoma [PMID:32805281, PMID:36605586, PMID:30782837].

BOP1 is a nucleolar WD40 repeat protein that serves as the central scaffold of the trimeric PeBoW complex (with Pes1 and WDR12), essential for processing of 32S pre-rRNA into mature 28S and 5.8S rRNAs and biogenesis of 60S ribosomal subunits [PMID:10891491, PMID:15225545, PMID:16043514]. BOP1 depletion or dominant-negative disruption triggers nucleolar stress that activates p53 through RPL11-mediated inhibition of MDM2, enforcing G1 cell cycle arrest independently of p19ARF [PMID:11390653, PMID:16043514, PMID:33510838, PMID:38409361]. Beyond ribosome biogenesis, BOP1 overexpression promotes epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition through RhoA activation, drives chromosomal instability via Aurora kinase B phosphorylation, and enhances Wnt/β-catenin signaling by recruiting CBP to acetylate β-catenin, thereby supporting cancer stem cell properties [PMID:21520196, PMID:32805281, PMID:33797754]. BOP1 protein stability is regulated by direct binding of lncRNAs CCAT2 and SNHG6, and BOP1 loss modulates MAPK signaling by downregulating DUSP4/DUSP6 phosphatases, conferring resistance to BRAF inhibitors in melanoma [PMID:32805281, PMID:36605586, PMID:30782837].

BRIX1 is a nucleolar ribosome biogenesis factor essential for assembly of the large (60S) ribosomal subunit. It binds 5S, 5.8S, and 28S rRNAs, supports formation of the PeBoW pre-60S assembly complex, and interacts with UBTF and POLR1A to drive rDNA transcription, with its own expression controlled by mTORC1–SP1 signaling [PMID:11843177, PMID:39475053, PMID:41370029]. BRIX1 depletion triggers nucleolar stress that activates p53 through the MDM2–RPL5/RPL11 surveillance pathway, and it suppresses SRSF1-dependent oncogenic alternative splicing downstream of ribosomal stress [PMID:39475053, PMID:41370029]. Beyond global translation, BRIX1 selectively enhances GLUT1 mRNA translation to promote glycolysis in colorectal cancer cells [PMID:38282151].

BUD23 is a conserved SAM-dependent N7-methylguanosine methyltransferase that, in obligate complex with TRMT112, methylates G1575 (yeast) / G1639 (human) on 18S rRNA during 40S ribosomal subunit biogenesis; however, its essential role in pre-rRNA processing, SSU Processome disassembly, and pre-40S nuclear export depends on its physical presence as a scaffold rather than its catalytic activity [PMID:18332120, PMID:25525153]. BUD23 is recruited to early nucleolar pre-ribosomes where it interacts with the DEAH helicase Dhr1/Ecm16 and a network of SSU Processome factors (Imp4, Utp2/Nop14, Bms1), promoting their coordinated disassembly, and is subsequently displaced from the maturing pre-40S particle by the atypical kinase Rio2 in a nucleotide-hydrolysis-independent manner [PMID:24710271, PMID:33306676, PMID:34934010]. In mammalian cells, BUD23-dependent ribosome programming selectively enhances translation of mRNAs with low 5′-UTR GC content, including mitochondrial transcripts, and cardiac-specific deletion in mice causes lethal cardiomyopathy due to mitochondrial dysfunction [PMID:31939735]. In C. elegans, BUD-23-mediated 18S rRNA m7G methylation is required for intergenerational epigenetic inheritance of stress resistance [PMID:37689068].

CCDC86 (Cyclon) is a cytokine-inducible, coiled-coil domain-containing nuclear protein that functions at the interface of ribosome biogenesis, chromosome periphery organization, and mitotic fidelity. During mitosis, CCDC86 localizes to the chromosome periphery where it forms subcomplexes with Ki-67, nucleolin, and NPM1 to regulate spindle length and kinetochore–microtubule attachments; its depletion causes chromosome alignment errors, cytoplasmic aggregation of perichromosomal components, and increased apoptosis [PMID:36695333]. In interphase, CCDC86 physically binds mRNA [PMID:22658674, PMID:22681889] and interacts with NPM1 to promote EGFR transcription and PI3K/Akt signaling in cancer cells, and with BHLHE40 to stabilize ATF3 expression and activate ERK-driven glycolysis in glioma [PMID:38247332, PMID:40837407]. In T cells, CCDC86 is induced by TCR ligation and promotes activation-induced cell death by upregulating Fas (CD95) expression, as demonstrated by conditional knockout and transgenic rescue of autoimmune pathology in IL-2R-deficient mice [PMID:19528538].

CENP-E is a kinesin-7 family plus-end-directed motor protein that functions as a central organizer of kinetochore–microtubule attachment, chromosome congression, and mitotic checkpoint signaling during cell division. It localizes to the fibrous corona of kinetochores from prometaphase through anaphase, where it transports pole-proximal chromosomes toward the metaphase plate along spindle microtubules, converts lateral kinetochore–microtubule attachments to stable end-on attachments through a tethered tip-tracking mechanism requiring both its N-terminal motor and C-terminal microtubule-binding domains, and directly activates BubR1 checkpoint kinase activity—silencing it upon microtubule capture in a ternary CENP-E–BubR1–microtubule complex that couples attachment status to checkpoint signaling [PMID:9363944, PMID:16144904, PMID:23955301, PMID:11030625]. CENP-E additionally recruits PP1 phosphatase and CLASP1/2 to kinetochores, delivers dynein–dynactin loading at the corona, and organizes PRC1 into the central spindle at mitotic exit [PMID:20691903, PMID:19733075, PMID:37984321, PMID:31174204]. Its activity and localization are regulated by autoinhibition relieved by Aurora A/B and CDK1 phosphorylation, SUMO-2/3 modification enabling kinetochore targeting via Nuf2 poly-SUMO chains, linear ubiquitination by LUBAC anchoring it to attached kinetochores through KNL1, and cell-cycle-dependent proteasomal degradation at M/G1 [PMID:18342609, PMID:37658044, PMID:18374647, PMID:33910471, PMID:30655516, PMID:8207059].

CTDP1 (FCP1) is a haloacid dehalogenase-family phosphatase that serves as the principal enzyme recycling RNA polymerase II between transcription rounds and as a mitotic exit coordinator. Its catalytic domain dephosphorylates the Pol II CTD heptad repeats via an aspartyl-phosphate intermediate, generating initiation-competent hypophosphorylated Pol II, while a separate interaction surface on Pol II stimulates transcription elongation; substrate selectivity extends to the Spt5 CTD, and an Arg271 residue governs Pol II versus Spt5 preference [PMID:9765293, PMID:19026779, PMID:25883047, PMID:22733996]. Recruitment to the transcription machinery depends on a disordered C-terminal helix that folds upon binding the RAP74 winged-helix domain of TFIIF, and CK2 phosphorylation at multiple sites (T584, S942/S944) is required for this interaction and for full phosphatase and elongation-stimulatory activity [PMID:12591941, PMID:12732728, PMID:12591939, PMID:15723518]. Independent of transcription, CTDP1 drives mitotic exit by dephosphorylating Greatwall kinase, Ensa/ARPP19, Cdc20, and Wee1, thereby coordinating CDK1 inactivation and PP2A-B55 reactivation, and it participates in DNA damage repair through BRCT-domain-mediated interaction with FANCI that promotes Fanconi anemia pathway foci formation and homologous recombination [PMID:22692537, PMID:26653855, PMID:31240132].

DDX18 is a nucleolar DEAD-box RNA helicase that couples ribosome biogenesis, R-loop resolution, and chromatin regulation to cell proliferation, genome stability, and stem cell pluripotency. It is a direct transcriptional target of Myc-Max and YY1, and its expression is linked to proliferative state across multiple cell types [PMID:8861962, PMID:40394670]. DDX18 maintains R-loop homeostasis in a PARP-1-dependent manner; its depletion causes aberrant R-loop accumulation, replication stress, and DNA damage that is rescued by RNase H1 overexpression [PMID:35858569]. In the nucleolus, DDX18 interacts with NPM1 to sustain nucleolar phase separation and perinucleolar heterochromatin organization required for human embryonic stem cell pluripotency [PMID:39738032], and it promotes cell-cycle progression by transcriptionally activating CDK4 and facilitating miR-21 maturation through interaction with Drosha [PMID:38732173, PMID:33489896].

DDX24 is a DEAD-box RNA helicase that functions as a multifaceted post-transcriptional and transcriptional regulator essential for ribosome biogenesis, vascular development, and innate immune homeostasis. DDX24 directly binds specific mRNAs—including LAMB1, FANCA, VEGFR2, PPFIA4, and IKBKG—to regulate their stability or alternative splicing, and promotes CCR4-NOT-dependent mRNA decay of endothelial transcripts such as CLEC14A and ERG to control angiogenesis [PMID:41728947, PMID:37470182, PMID:40339127, PMID:39897555]. In the nucleolus, MDM2-mediated nonproteolytic polyubiquitylation of DDX24 facilitates its association with pre-rRNP complexes required for pre-rRNA processing, and DDX24 regulates nucleolar organization through NPM1-dependent liquid–liquid phase separation [PMID:24980433, PMID:37705750]. DDX24 additionally suppresses p53 activation by inhibiting p300-mediated p53 acetylation, attenuates RLR-mediated type I interferon responses by associating with FADD and RIP1, and is itself subject to TRIM27-mediated proteasomal degradation counteracted by the lncRNA LINC02551 [PMID:25867071, PMID:24204270, PMID:36335087].

DDX47 is a nucleolar DEAD-box RNA helicase that functions in ribosome biogenesis and R-loop resolution to maintain translational capacity and genome integrity. It possesses RNA-independent ATPase activity and RNA binding capability, localizes to the nucleolus in a NOP132-dependent manner, and associates with pre-rRNA precursors as a component of the small subunit processome (SSUP), where it promotes 18S rRNA maturation and sustains global translation rates critical for maintaining pluripotency factor levels in embryonic stem cells [PMID:16963496, PMID:26443847, PMID:11024137]. DDX47 also functions as an R-loop resolvase, recruited to R-loop-containing chromatin by FANCD2 during replication stress, where it cooperates with SETX and DDX39B to suppress R-loop accumulation—particularly at nucleolar loci—thereby preventing transcription-replication collisions and preserving genome stability [PMID:36827184, PMID:30431240]. DDX47 additionally interacts with GABARAP, and their co-expression induces apoptosis in tumor cells [PMID:15977068].

DDX56 is a nucleolar DEAD-box RNA helicase with ATPase activity that plays essential, conserved roles in 60S ribosomal subunit assembly, nucleolar integrity, and innate immune regulation, while also being co-opted by multiple viruses during infection. In its constitutive function, DDX56 resides in the nucleolus as a component of 65S preribosomal particles, where it is required for rRNA processing, ribosome biogenesis, and stem cell viability across species from planarians to mammals [PMID:10749921, PMID:33789112, PMID:32703285]. During viral infections, DDX56 relocalizes from the nucleolus to the cytoplasm, where it can either promote viral replication—by facilitating flavivirus virion assembly through helicase-dependent interaction with capsid protein at ER assembly sites [PMID:21411523, PMID:22925334, PMID:27821284]—or restrict infection by directly binding and destabilizing alphavirus genomic RNA [PMID:33109765]; DDX56 also modulates type I interferon signaling by targeting importins KPNA3/KPNA4 to block IRF3 nuclear translocation or by activating the cGAS–STING pathway, depending on viral context [PMID:34922148, PMID:36090064]. Beyond ribosome biogenesis and immunity, DDX56 participates in transcriptional and post-transcriptional gene regulation: it interacts with Sox2 in the Oct4/Sox2 complex in embryonic stem cells, cooperates with MECOM to promote H3K9me1-dependent MIST1 transcription in hepatocellular carcinoma, and facilitates pri-miRNA degradation to derepress Wnt signaling targets in lung cancer [PMID:32703285, PMID:36168636, PMID:34446021].

DHX37 is a DEAH-box RNA helicase essential for small ribosomal subunit biogenesis, functioning by ATP-dependent 3′-to-5′ translocation to displace U3 snoRNA from pre-rRNA, thereby enabling central pseudoknot formation in nascent pre-40S particles [PMID:25710520, PMID:30582406]. Its helicase activity is autoinhibited by its N-terminus and an internal RecA2 loop, and is specifically activated by the cofactor UTP14A, which binds the RecA1/RecA2 domains to stimulate ATPase activity and RNA engagement; a structurally unique C-terminal domain is additionally required for UTP14A interaction and ribosome biogenesis in vivo [PMID:30910870, PMID:40024476]. Beyond ribosome assembly, DHX37 resolves transcription-associated R-loops to prevent replication stress and DNA damage [PMID:40043837], interacts with PLRG1 to co-activate CCND1 transcription at superenhancers in hepatocellular carcinoma cells [PMID:35290436], and is required in Sertoli cells for nucleolar integrity and PI3K-AKT/p53 signaling, with its conditional loss causing spermatogenic failure [PMID:41535247]. Mutations in DHX37 are associated with 46,XY disorders of sex development and microcephaly, with disease-linked variants impairing ribosome biogenesis or altering RNA target networks in gonadal cells [PMID:31188444, PMID:38769888].

DIMT1 is a conserved S-adenosylmethionine-dependent dimethyladenosine transferase that installs N6,N6-dimethyladenosine (m6,6A) modifications on two adjacent adenosines near the 3′ end of 18S rRNA, functioning as both a catalytic enzyme and an essential structural scaffold in small ribosomal subunit biogenesis. The protein scaffold, mediated by a positively charged RNA-binding cleft distinct from the catalytic site, is required for pre-rRNA processing, 40S subunit assembly, nucleolar localization via liquid–liquid phase separation, and cell proliferation, independent of methyltransferase activity [PMID:25851604, PMID:32616653, PMID:37024283]. The catalytic activity is separately required for translational fidelity and also modifies small RNAs, contributing to protein synthesis and cell viability [PMID:32616653, PMID:34473991]. In C. elegans, the DIMT-1 ortholog mediates intergenerational rRNA methylation changes in response to parental starvation and regulates lifespan through germline-specific translational reprogramming [PMID:37689068, PMID:40721431].

EIF1AD is a late-acting 40S ribosome biogenesis factor that binds to pre-40S ribosomal particles near RIOK1 and the central rRNA helix 44, where it is required for efficient assembly factor recycling and 18S-E pre-rRNA processing during the final steps of human 40S ribosome maturation [PMID:33208940]. Structural analysis shows that EIF1AD conserves ribosome-binding surfaces equivalent to those of its paralog eIF1A, including a nearly invariant surface-exposed tryptophan residue critical for ribosome interaction [PMID:30180896].

EIF2B3 encodes the γ subunit of eIF2B, a heterodecameric guanine nucleotide exchange factor (GEF) that catalyzes GDP-to-GTP exchange on eIF2, a rate-limiting step in translation initiation [PMID:7893825, PMID:29599213]. The γ subunit contributes to holoenzyme assembly through its pyrophosphorylase-like and left-handed β-helix domains, which form extensive contacts with the catalytic ε subunit [PMID:22238343]; catalytic GEF activity resides in the ε subunit and is regulated by eIF2α phosphorylation (converting eIF2 into a competitive inhibitor of eIF2B), by GSK-3–mediated phosphorylation of ε Ser-535, and by ISRIB binding at the β–δ interface that promotes decameric assembly [PMID:7565788, PMID:8007958, PMID:25858979, PMID:29599245]. Loss-of-function mutations in EIF2B3 cause vanishing white matter disease (leukoencephalopathy), characterized by defective myelination, impaired integrated stress responses, and dysregulated autophagy in oligodendrocytes [PMID:11835386, PMID:33517449, PMID:26625702].

EIF6 is a ribosome anti-association factor that binds free cytoplasmic 60S ribosomal subunits and prevents premature 80S ribosome assembly, thereby serving as a gatekeeper for translational activation [PMID:14654845]. Release of EIF6 from the 60S subunit is catalyzed by the SBDS–EFL1 GTPase machinery through a GTP hydrolysis–dependent mechanism; disease-associated SBDS mutations uncouple GTP hydrolysis from EIF6 eviction, establishing Shwachman-Diamond syndrome as a ribosomopathy of defective EIF6 release [PMID:21536732]. EIF6 release is also regulated by RACK1-scaffolded PKC phosphorylation of a critical C-terminal serine, and RACK1/PKC signaling can rescue EIF6-imposed translational blocks [PMID:14654845]. Beyond canonical translation, EIF6 associates with the RISC complex and is required for miRNA-mediated post-transcriptional silencing in both human cells and C. elegans [PMID:17507929].

EP400 is the SWI2/SNF2-family ATPase subunit of the TIP60/NuA4 chromatin remodeling complex, functioning as a central integrator of histone variant exchange, transcriptional regulation, DNA repair, and cell fate determination. EP400 uses ATP hydrolysis to exchange canonical histones H2A and H3.1 for variants H2A.Z and H3.3 at gene promoters and enhancers, thereby modulating chromatin accessibility and transcriptional output in cooperation with TIP60 acetyltransferase activity; it is recruited to target loci through H3K4me3 recognition and interactions with transcription factors including Nanog, Sox10, NFYA, and MYCL [PMID:26669263, PMID:18614019, PMID:31081019, PMID:38493496]. At DNA double-strand breaks, EP400 destabilizes nucleosomes in an ATPase- and Tip60-dependent manner to enable RNF8-mediated ubiquitination and recruitment of BRCA1, 53BP1, and Rad51 for homologous recombination, while suppressing error-prone alternative end joining [PMID:20876283, PMID:23266955, PMID:26578561]. EP400 represses p21 transcription to promote cell cycle progression, compensates for SWI/SNF loss by maintaining promoter accessibility (creating a synthetic lethal relationship), co-localizes with paused RNA Pol II at transcription start sites to regulate elongation, and is essential for zygotic genome activation, hematopoiesis, myelination, and Schwann cell differentiation [PMID:15655109, PMID:37922899, PMID:40842241, PMID:20610385, PMID:31142747].

ESF1 is an evolutionarily conserved nucleolar protein essential for 18S rRNA biogenesis and early pre-rRNA processing. In yeast, Esf1p associates with ribosomal proteins, U3 and U14 snoRNAs, and functions as an accessory factor (not a core SSU processome subunit) required for efficient 35S pre-rRNA processing and 18S rRNA accumulation [PMID:15056729]; in human cells, ESF1 associates specifically with pre-40S ribosomal particles and facilitates pre-rRNA conformational maturation rather than direct cleavage [PMID:38391939]. Loss of esf1 in zebrafish triggers ribosome biogenesis stress that activates p53-dependent apoptosis, causing neural crest–derived craniofacial and organ defects that are rescued by p53 inactivation [PMID:30073783]. In human cancer cells, ESF1 additionally stabilizes MDM2 by inhibiting its ubiquitination, thereby suppressing p53 signaling and promoting cell proliferation, migration, and tumorigenesis [PMID:38971273].

FAU encodes a ubiquitously expressed fusion protein comprising the ubiquitin-like modifier FUBI at the N-terminus and ribosomal protein eS30 at the C-terminus, with these two domains serving distinct cellular functions [PMID:1326960, PMID:8395683]. Proteolytic cleavage of FUBI from eS30 by the deubiquitinases USP36 and USP16 is essential for cytoplasmic 40S ribosomal subunit maturation and 18S rRNA processing [PMID:34318747, PMID:37443395]. Free FUBI functions as a ubiquitin-like modifier that covalently conjugates via its C-terminal Gly74 to substrates including Bcl-G, endophilin II, FDH, HSP60, and IGF2BP2, thereby promoting caspase-dependent apoptosis through a Bcl-G-dependent pathway, modulating macrophage inflammatory signaling via ERK/AP-1 and NF-κB cascades, regulating trophoblast invasion, and directing F508del-CFTR for degradation [PMID:16621790, PMID:23298187, PMID:21550398, PMID:20849826, PMID:26192119, PMID:34668606, PMID:29158263]. FUBI also regulates TNFα production by sequestering RC3H1 into stress granules, and di-FUBI chains inhibit UCHL3 deubiquitinase activity, revealing an expanding ubiquitin-like signaling network [PMID:39260307, PMID:40464359].

GNL2 (NGP-1/Nog2) is a nucleolar GTP-binding protein essential for 60S ribosomal subunit maturation and cell cycle progression. It localizes to the nucleolus via dual importin-α/β-dependent nucleolar localization signals gated by GTP binding and active transcription, and its GTPase activity is regulated by rRNA A-loop methylation status, establishing a kinetic checkpoint at the nucleolar–nucleoplasmic boundary that controls pre-60S particle release [PMID:21495629, PMID:36864048]. GNL2 promotes G1-to-S phase transition through a p53/p21–cyclin D1–CDK4/Rb/E2F1 axis, with the ribosomal protein RPL23A counterbalancing GNL2-induced p53 activity via enhanced Mdm2-mediated p53 degradation [PMID:26203195, PMID:21565180]. GNL2 silencing impairs global protein synthesis and cell proliferation in ovarian cancer and glioma models, linking its ribosome biogenesis function to oncogenic growth [PMID:34965383, PMID:38779136].

GNL3L is a nucleolar GTPase of the HSR1/MMR1 family that functions as a central regulator of ribosome biogenesis and cell cycle progression. Its GTPase activity, driven by circularly permuted G-motifs, is required for pre-60S rRNA processing, 60S subunit maintenance, and protein synthesis, while a lysine-rich nucleolar localization signal and GTP binding cooperate for nucleolar retention [PMID:16251348, PMID:41755636, PMID:17034816]. In the nucleoplasm, GNL3L stabilizes TRF1 by blocking FBX4-mediated ubiquitylation to promote the metaphase-to-anaphase transition, and stabilizes MDM2 by preventing its ubiquitylation to suppress p53 target gene expression and G2/M arrest [PMID:19487455, PMID:21132010]. GNL3L additionally inhibits ERRγ transcription by competing with SRC coactivators, activates NF-κB signaling through modulation of p65, and promotes autophagy via the AMPK pathway [PMID:17623774, PMID:27764577, PMID:38148364].

HEATR1 is a conserved nucleolar HEAT-repeat protein essential for ribosomal RNA transcription and early pre-rRNA processing, functioning as a component of the U3 snoRNP/SSU processome required for 18S rRNA maturation [PMID:16531401, PMID:17652137, PMID:29143558]. Loss of HEATR1 disrupts nucleolar integrity and activates the RPL5/RPL11–MDM2 ribosome biogenesis stress checkpoint, stabilizing p53 and triggering p53-dependent cell cycle arrest, apoptosis via PUMA/BAX, and ferroptosis through the p53/SAT1/ALOX15 axis [PMID:29143558, PMID:31190896, PMID:38818906]. Beyond ribosome biogenesis, HEATR1 serves as a scaffold bridging AKT and PP2A to promote AKT dephosphorylation, competes with Keap1 for p62/SQSTM1 binding to restrain Nrf2 signaling, stabilizes the Pontin/Reptin chaperone complex, and binds MYC to direct its nucleolar localization and MYC-driven rRNA synthesis [PMID:26676747, PMID:31785531, PMID:33894417, PMID:38225354].

ISG20L2 is a vertebrate-specific nucleolar 3'-to-5' exoribonuclease of the DEDDh/RNase T superfamily that plays essential roles in ribosome biogenesis and immune regulation. Its crystal structure reveals a DEDDh active site (Asp183, Glu185, Asp267, His322, Asp327) with an αβα fold; loss-of-function studies demonstrate that it processes multiple pre-rRNA intermediates—removing the 3' external transcribed spacer (3'ETS), trimming ITS1 after endonucleolytic cleavage during 18S maturation, contributing to ITS2/5.8S 3'-end maturation, and processing the U8 snoRNA precursor—and its inactivation impairs large ribosomal subunit formation, disorganizes the nucleolar dense fibrillar component, and reduces cell proliferation [PMID:38153123, PMID:41261865]. Outside the nucleolus, ISG20L2 is upregulated by TCR and type I interferon stimulation in T lymphocytes, where it preferentially degrades uridylated miRNA substrates and regulates immune synapse formation and expression of immunomodulatory receptors including PD-1, CTLA-4, and NKG2D [PMID:37646974]. ISG20L2 also directly binds bortezomib and competes with the proteasome subunit PSMB5, conferring proteasome-inhibitor resistance in multiple myeloma cells [PMID:36040812].

KRI1 (Protein KRI1 homolog) functions in 18S rRNA processing and 40S ribosomal subunit biogenesis as a nucleolar assembly factor. In yeast, Kri1p physically interacts with Krr1p via its divergent KH1 domain, and depletion of Kri1p abolishes 18S rRNA production and destabilizes 20S pre-rRNA precursors without affecting 25S rRNA [PMID:11027267, PMID:24990943]. Cryo-EM analysis of the 90S pre-ribosome reveals that Kri1 forms part of a Krr1–Utp23–Kri1 assembly module recruited by the snR30 snoRNP to coordinate integration of a pre-18S rRNA platform subdomain containing helices and ES6 [PMID:40399280]. The C. elegans ortholog KRI-1 (also designated the KRIT1/CCM1 ortholog) operates in the intestine in a complex with CCM-2 to negatively regulate ERK-5/MAPK signaling and control zinc homeostasis via KLF-3–dependent zipt-2.3 expression, non-cell-autonomously enabling DNA damage–induced germline apoptosis and, through generation of H₂S and ROS, activating SKN-1/Nrf2 and the mitochondrial UPR to promote longevity [PMID:30996251, PMID:27140632, PMID:20137949].

LSG1 is a conserved circularly permuted GTPase that functions at a late cytoplasmic step of 60S ribosomal subunit maturation, coupling GTP hydrolysis to the release of the nuclear export adapter NMD3 and thereby recycling NMD3 back to the nucleus for further rounds of pre-60S export [PMID:15660131, PMID:28112732]. This reaction requires the ribosomal protein Rpl10/uL16, whose central loop (residues 102–112) is specifically needed for LSG1-dependent NMD3 eviction, and the Nmd3–60S complex acts as a GTP-stabilizing factor that keeps LSG1 in its active, GTP-bound state [PMID:17761675, PMID:32916301]. Independently of its ribosome maturation role, human LSG1 localizes to the endoplasmic reticulum through a VAP-binding FFAT-like motif; disruption of this motif abolishes ER tethering without impairing NMD3 recycling, and LSG1 inhibition triggers ER stress and cellular senescence via upregulation of cholesterol biosynthesis rather than translational insufficiency [PMID:39133101, PMID:31148378].

LTV1 is a conserved assembly factor for the 40S ribosomal subunit that chaperones hierarchical incorporation of head ribosomal proteins (Rps3, Rps10, Asc1/RACK1) and directs rRNA folding during small subunit maturation [PMID:30348748, PMID:37910572]. It contains a C-terminal CRM1-dependent nuclear export sequence that couples pre-40S subunit export to cytoplasmic maturation; dominant-negative NES mutations trap pre-40S particles and block recycling of late assembly factors such as Tsr1 [PMID:16888326, PMID:20215468, PMID:25213169]. Phosphorylation of Ltv1 by casein kinase 1δ/ε (Hrr25 in yeast) triggers its release from nascent 40S subunits and permits entry into a translation-like quality-control cycle [PMID:25778921]. Biallelic loss-of-function variants in human LTV1 cause LIPHAK syndrome, a ribosomopathy featuring inflammatory poikiloderma and acral keratoses, confirming its essential role in ribosome biogenesis [PMID:34999892].

LTV1 is a conserved assembly factor for the 40S ribosomal subunit that chaperones hierarchical incorporation of head ribosomal proteins (Rps3, Rps10, Asc1/RACK1) and directs rRNA folding during small subunit maturation [PMID:30348748, PMID:37910572]. It contains a C-terminal CRM1-dependent nuclear export sequence that couples pre-40S subunit export to cytoplasmic maturation; dominant-negative NES mutations trap pre-40S particles and block recycling of late assembly factors such as Tsr1 [PMID:16888326, PMID:20215468, PMID:25213169]. Phosphorylation of Ltv1 by casein kinase 1δ/ε (Hrr25 in yeast) triggers its release from nascent 40S subunits and permits entry into a translation-like quality-control cycle [PMID:25778921]. Biallelic loss-of-function variants in human LTV1 cause LIPHAK syndrome, a ribosomopathy featuring inflammatory poikiloderma and acral keratoses, confirming its essential role in ribosome biogenesis [PMID:34999892].

MAK16 is a conserved nucleolar assembly factor essential for large ribosomal subunit biogenesis. It functions within the Nsa1/Rrp1/Rpf1/Mak16 module (WDR74/RPF1/MAK16/RRP1 in humans) to stabilize the solvent-exposed face of the nascent pre-60S particle, and is required for 27SB pre-rRNA stability and maturation of 25S and 5.8S rRNAs [PMID:16710831, PMID:29245012, PMID:39706051]. MAK16 coordinates a redox-active [4Fe-4S] iron–sulfur cluster that is essential for protein stability, for its physical interaction with Rpf1, and for maintaining 25S rRNA levels; oxidative stress converts this cluster to a [3Fe-4S] form and disrupts the Mak16–Rpf1 interaction in vivo, thereby coupling cellular redox status to ribosome assembly [PMID:41231949]. Nucleolar targeting is directed by conserved nuclear localization signals and the protein is phosphorylated by casein kinase CK2, features conserved from yeast to metazoans [PMID:3045810, PMID:10838225].

MCM5 is a core subunit of the MCM2-7 replicative helicase complex essential for DNA replication initiation and elongation in eukaryotes. Within the hexameric ring, MCM5 forms a regulated gate with MCM2 that controls DNA entry during origin licensing; this Mcm2/5 interface is remodeled to a closed state during ORC-Cdc6-Cdt1-mediated loading, and MCM5 serves as a key regulatory target of DDK kinase (Cdc7-Dbf4), whose requirement can be bypassed by the MCM5-P83L conformational mutation [PMID:17895243, PMID:39747125, PMID:9096361]. UFMylation of MCM5 at Lys583 by UFL1 stabilizes the CMG helicase complex and is required for efficient origin firing and fork progression [PMID:40940420]. Beyond replication, MCM5 directly binds STAT1 via residues R732/K734 and is recruited to cytokine-responsive gene promoters where it is essential for STAT1-mediated transcription activation and T cell survival through a Stat1-Bcl2 axis; it also interacts with cyclins A/E at centrosomes to prevent reduplication, and biallelic loss-of-function mutations cause Meier-Gorlin syndrome [PMID:11248027, PMID:16199513, PMID:39929806, PMID:18799789, PMID:28198391].

MDM2 is the principal E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase governing p53 stability and transcriptional activity, forming an autoregulatory negative-feedback loop in which p53 transcriptionally induces MDM2, which in turn ubiquitinates p53 for proteasomal degradation [PMID:9153396, PMID:9450543]. The MDM2 N-terminal hydrophobic cleft engages the p53 transactivation-domain helix (Phe19, Trp23, Leu26), while the C-terminal RING domain provides E3 ligase activity; heterodimerization of the MDM2 RING with MDMX converts MDM2 from a mono- to a polyubiquitination ligase, and dose-dependent ubiquitin chain length dictates whether p53 is exported from the nucleus or degraded in situ [PMID:8875929, PMID:14671306, PMID:22134240]. This feedback circuit is tuned by upstream signals including ARF-mediated nucleolar sequestration of MDM2, Akt phosphorylation of MDM2 Ser166/186 promoting nuclear entry, ribosomal stress proteins (RPL5, RPL11, RPL23, RPL6) that inhibit MDM2 E3 activity, and Daxx/HAUSP-mediated MDM2 stabilization [PMID:9529249, PMID:11504915, PMID:12842086, PMID:16845383]. Beyond p53, MDM2 ubiquitinates HIF-1α, MDMX, Ku70, and β-arrestin, interacts with pRB and Nbs1 to modulate cell-cycle control and DNA repair, and associates with polycomb repressive complexes to regulate chromatin [PMID:10640274, PMID:7691904, PMID:18541670, PMID:27927750].

MRTO4 is a trans-acting ribosome assembly factor that occupies the ribosomal P0-binding site on pre-60S particles to regulate the timing and fidelity of stalk assembly during large ribosomal subunit biogenesis. As a structural paralogue of P0, MRTO4 binds the 25S/28S rRNA GAR domain through its N-terminal domain, preventing premature P0 loading; in the cytoplasm, the phosphatase Yvh1 displaces MRTO4 from pre-60S subunits to allow P0 incorporation and mature stalk formation [PMID:19346338, PMID:19797078, PMID:20083226]. MRTO4 localizes predominantly to the nucleolus via rRNA interaction, shuttles between nucleus and cytoplasm, and its C-terminal serines are phosphorylated by CK2 to modulate its behavior during nucleolar stress [PMID:20083226, PMID:26494001]. An additional cytoplasmic role has been described in hepatocellular carcinoma cells, where MRTO4 promotes glycolysis by inhibiting aldolase B (ALDOB) [PMID:38778508].

MTREX (MTR4/SKIV2L2) is a nuclear DExH-box RNA helicase that serves as the central ATP-dependent unwinding engine and adaptor scaffold for the RNA exosome, channeling diverse RNA substrates—including pre-rRNAs, noncoding RNAs, aberrant mRNAs, replication-dependent histone mRNAs, and retrotransposon transcripts—into the exosome for processing or degradation. Its helicase core unwinds structured and polyadenylated RNA substrates, while a distinctive arch/KOW domain simultaneously contacts structured RNA and recruits adaptor proteins through short arch-interacting motifs (AIMs), enabling assembly of functionally distinct complexes: TRAMP (with Trf4/Air2), NEXT (with ZCCHC8/RBM7), and PAXT (with ZFC3H1), as well as ribosome biogenesis factors such as NOP53 and NVL2 [PMID:20566885, PMID:28883156, PMID:29844170, PMID:28733371, PMID:31358741]. MTR4 is recruited to the exosome core through composite surfaces formed by MPP6 and RRP6/RRP47, and RNA-engaged MTR4 threads substrates through the exosome central channel to the DIS3 active site; the negative regulator NRDE2 locks MTR4 in a closed conformation that blocks exosome recruitment [PMID:29906447, PMID:25319414, PMID:30842217]. Beyond RNA turnover, MTR4 controls nuclear RNA export, alternative splicing of metabolic and meiotic transcripts, R-loop resolution, subnuclear localization of exosome subunits, and chromatin state in oocytes and germ cells, with conditional knockout in mice causing infertility due to blocked meiotic initiation and oocyte growth failure [PMID:39378876, PMID:40097464, PMID:32024842, PMID:40651665].

RMP64 (NEPRO) is a nucleolar protein that functions as a constitutive, metazoan-specific subunit of the RNase MRP ribonucleoprotein complex, distinguishing it from the closely related RNase P complex. RMP64, together with RMP24 (C18orf21), stabilizes the MRP catalytic RNA, is essential for pre-rRNA ITS1 site 2 cleavage, and is preferentially required for 40S ribosome biogenesis; cryo-EM structures reveal a 'double-anchor' substrate-binding mechanism and confirm RMP64 as indispensable for precursor-rRNA cleavage and ribosome assembly [PMID:40413743, PMID:40867056, PMID:41136609, PMID:41888142]. Nuclear import of RMP64 depends on a bipartite NLS (aa 74–96) recognized by importin-α1, and the disease-associated R94C mutation abolishes nuclear localization, reduces polysome abundance, and impairs cell proliferation [PMID:41652993]. Biallelic pathogenic variants in NEPRO cause a skeletal ribosomopathy overlapping cartilage-hair hypoplasia, and loss of Nepro in mouse embryos disrupts nucleolar function, triggers p53-dependent apoptosis, and blocks blastocyst formation, while in the developing neocortex Nepro acts downstream of Notch signaling—independently of Hes factors—to maintain neural progenitor cells by repressing proneural gene expression [PMID:31250547, PMID:26178919, PMID:19906856].

NFS1 is a pyridoxal phosphate-dependent cysteine desulfurase that provides inorganic sulfur for iron-sulfur (Fe/S) cluster biogenesis and related sulfur-requiring pathways in both mitochondria and the cytosol. It catalyzes the desulfurization of L-cysteine to L-alanine via an active-site cysteine persulfide intermediate (Cys325 in human), operating within a core mitochondrial complex with ISD11 (which prevents NFS1 aggregation and modulates its oligomeric state), the scaffold protein ISCU (which receives the persulfide sulfur), and frataxin (which accelerates persulfide transfer to ISCU) [PMID:8464885, PMID:16341090, PMID:25597503, PMID:21298097]. In the cytosol, NFS1 donates sulfur to MOCS3 for molybdenum cofactor biosynthesis [PMID:18650437, PMID:23593335]. NFS1 is essential for maintaining Fe/S co-factor integrity under high-oxygen conditions, and its loss triggers ferroptosis through iron-starvation signaling; phosphorylation at S293 modulates cell death sensitivity, and biallelic NFS1 mutations cause infantile mitochondrial complex II/III deficiency in humans [PMID:29168506, PMID:35221331, PMID:24498631].

NIFK is a nucleolar RRM-containing RNA-binding phosphoprotein that functions in pre-ribosomal RNA processing and cell cycle progression. It binds the 5′-region of ITS2 rRNA in a sequence- and structure-dependent manner via its RRM domain, and this RNA-binding activity is essential for ITS1 cleavage and maturation of 28S and 5.8S rRNA; loss of NIFK triggers RPL5/RPL11-mediated nucleolar stress and p53-dependent G1 arrest [PMID:25826659]. NIFK interacts with the Ki-67 FHA domain in a mitosis-specific, phosphorylation-dependent manner through a pThr234-Pro235 motif, and co-localizes with Ki-67 at the periphery of mitotic chromosomes [PMID:11342549, PMID:14659764]. In cancer, NIFK drives metastasis by repressing RUNX1-dependent CK1α expression to activate TCF4/β-catenin signaling, and promotes proliferation through the MYC pathway [PMID:26984280, PMID:37950567].

NLE1 is a WD40-repeat nucleolar protein that functions in ribosome biogenesis and de novo protein synthesis, and positively modulates Notch1 signaling by forming a physical complex with Notch1 [PMID:12429849, PMID:39423824]. In colorectal cancer cells, NLE1 is transcriptionally upregulated by c-MYC binding an E-box in its promoter downstream of SMAD4 loss; its ablation impairs protein biosynthesis, activates p38/MAPK signaling, disrupts autophagy, elevates reactive oxygen species, and suppresses tumor growth and metastasis in orthotopic models [PMID:36219392]. Across multiple cancer contexts—melanoma, non-small-cell lung cancer, and glioblastoma stem cells—NLE1 promotes proliferation and migration through PI3K/AKT pathway engagement and E2F1-mediated transcriptional activation of CDK1, and its pharmacological targeting by edaravone impairs Notch signaling and sensitizes brain tumor stem cells to radiation [PMID:34019907, PMID:36818671, PMID:39423824].

NMD3 is a conserved nucleocytoplasmic shuttling adaptor that mediates CRM1/RanGTP-dependent nuclear export of pre-60S ribosomal subunits and serves as a structural checkpoint for peptidyl-transferase center (PTC) maturation. NMD3 binds the intersubunit face of the nascent 60S subunit near the PTC in its near-mature conformation, recognizing correct PTC assembly before recruiting CRM1 via a leucine-rich nuclear export signal for translocation through the nuclear pore complex [PMID:12773398, PMID:28112732, PMID:20584915]. Cytoplasmic release of NMD3 from the 60S subunit requires the ribosomal protein uL16 (Rpl10) and the GTPase Lsg1, and is coupled to the Efl1–Sdo1 axis that also drives Tif6 release; failure to dislodge NMD3 from the P site—as occurs with the T-ALL-associated rpl10-R98S mutation—blocks late cytoplasmic maturation [PMID:17015443, PMID:28715419]. NMD3 thereby functions as a quality-control gatekeeper that prevents structurally defective 60S subunits from entering the translating pool [PMID:28715419, PMID:10022925].

NOB1 is a conserved PIN-domain endonuclease essential for the final step of small ribosomal subunit biogenesis, catalyzing cleavage of 20S pre-rRNA at site D to generate the mature 3'-end of 18S rRNA. Its PIN domain carries the Mn²⁺-dependent catalytic active site and mediates substrate binding at the single-stranded cleavage site, while a zinc ribbon domain anchors the enzyme to helix 40 of small subunit rRNA, as demonstrated by NMR structure and mutagenesis of the archaeal ortholog [PMID:15388878, PMID:19706509, PMID:22156373]. In yeast, Nob1 catalytic activity at site D is coordinated with the DEAH-box helicase Prp43 and its cofactor Pfa1 through a genetically defined epistatic pathway [PMID:19801658], and Nob1 separately functions as a chaperone in 26S proteasome assembly by facilitating joining of the 19S regulatory particle with the 20S core, after which it is internalized and degraded [PMID:12502737]. In human cells, NOB1 proximity interactors are enriched in ribosome assembly and translation factors including EIF4B and EIF4G2 [PMID:40157618], and NOB1 silencing in multiple cancer cell types suppresses proliferation, induces apoptosis, and modulates MAPK/JNK signaling [PMID:23911301, PMID:27035645].

NOL8 (Nop132) is a phosphorylated, RRM domain-containing nucleolar protein that functions in ribosome biogenesis by recruiting pre-rRNA processing factors to transcriptionally active nucleolar regions [PMID:16963496, PMID:14660641]. It associates in a GTP-dependent manner with Rag family GTPases (RRAG A/C/D) and with the ribosome biogenesis factor Nip7, and physically interacts with the DEAD-box helicase DDX47, whose proper nucleolar localization depends on NOL8 [PMID:14660641, PMID:16963496]. NOL8 also binds β-catenin, enhances the β-catenin–TCF4 interaction, and activates Wnt/β-catenin transcriptional signaling; loss of NOL8 impairs cell growth and can induce apoptosis [PMID:30125550, PMID:15132771].

NOP16 (HSPC111) is a nucleolar protein that participates in ribosome biogenesis and epigenetic regulation of gene expression. It resides in a large RNA-dependent nucleolar complex where it directly interacts with RTCD1/RTCA to synergistically regulate rRNA synthesis, ribosome assembly, and cell growth, with its transcription controlled by c-Myc via E-box elements [PMID:18373870, PMID:24425784]. NOP16 also functions as an endogenous histone H3K27 mimic by binding EED (PRC2) and the demethylase JMJD3, competing with histone H3 for H3K27 methylation/demethylation machinery; its depletion globally increases H3K27me3 and causes cell cycle arrest with selective loss of E2F target gene expression [PMID:37397991]. In colorectal cancer, exosomal NOP16 phosphorylates ATP-citrate lyase (ACLY) in cancer-associated fibroblasts, elevating acetyl-CoA and H3K27 acetylation at the CXCL5 promoter to establish a pro-metastatic CXCL5–CXCR2 signaling loop [PMID:35027547].

NOP2 (NSUN1/p120) is an S-adenosyl-methionine-dependent RNA:m5C methyltransferase essential for ribosome biogenesis that catalyzes 5-methylcytosine deposition at position C4447 of 28S rRNA (C2870 in yeast 25S rRNA) and, independently of its catalytic activity, promotes 60S large ribosomal subunit assembly by facilitating recruitment of box C/D snoRNPs (U3, U8) to pre-ribosomal particles during pre-rRNA processing [PMID:36161484, PMID:26196125, PMID:11452018]. NOP2 binds rRNA through an N-terminal arginine-rich domain and associates with 60–80S pre-ribosomal particles in the nucleolus [PMID:9531475, PMID:7806561]. Loss of the rRNA m5C modification in C. elegans selectively remodels mRNA translation without reducing global protein synthesis, indicating that NOP2-deposited m5C tunes translational specificity [PMID:33289480]. In cancer cells, NOP2 additionally methylates mRNA substrates including c-Myc and EZH2, regulating their stability and downstream glycolytic and epithelial–mesenchymal transition programs [PMID:37398932, PMID:39013911].

NPM1 is a multifunctional nucleolar phosphoprotein that integrates ribosome biogenesis, centrosome duplication, p53 regulation, and transcriptional control. It possesses intrinsic ribonuclease activity for pre-rRNA processing and molecular chaperone activity that prevents protein aggregation and promotes refolding, while also chaperoning NF-κB p65 to enhance its DNA-binding capacity [PMID:7479045, PMID:10211837, PMID:28003476]. NPM1 governs centrosome duplication through CDK2/cyclin E-mediated Thr199 phosphorylation that recruits ROCK II, Plk1-mediated Ser4 phosphorylation during mitosis, and Plk2-mediated Ser4 phosphorylation during S-phase, while Aurora kinase phosphorylation at Ser125 directs its midbody localization for cytokinesis [PMID:17015463, PMID:15190079, PMID:20352051, PMID:24857377]. NPM1 controls p53 stability by sequestering ARF in the nucleolus — an interaction disrupted by DNA damage to permit ARF–MDM2 complex formation — and via SIRT7-dependent deacetylation that triggers NPM1 translocation to the nucleoplasm where it binds MDM2 and blocks p53 ubiquitination; the leukemia-associated cytoplasmic mutant NPM1c acquires a neomorphic chromatin-binding function at HOXA/B and MEIS1 loci in cooperation with MLL1, and its cytoplasmic localization is required to maintain the AML leukemic state [PMID:14729947, PMID:16267006, PMID:33495326, PMID:36455613, PMID:30205049].

PCF11 is a conserved core subunit of the cleavage/polyadenylation machinery that couples RNA polymerase II transcription termination to 3'-end processing of mRNAs and non-coding RNAs. Its N-terminal CTD-interaction domain (CID) binds phosphorylated Pol II CTD repeats by induced fit, enabling PCF11 to bridge the polymerase to the nascent transcript and dismantle elongation complexes without nucleotide hydrolysis—a mechanism conserved from yeast to metazoans [PMID:15998810, PMID:16387654, PMID:15665873]. PCF11 operates genome-wide at sub-stoichiometric levels relative to the CPA complex: it stimulates premature cleavage/polyadenylation to attenuate transcriptional regulators, autoregulates its own abundance via intronic polyadenylation, and modulates alternative polyadenylation in a gene-size-dependent manner, with functional consequences for neurodifferentiation and HIV-1 latency [PMID:30819644, PMID:30840896, PMID:30552333, PMID:38015843]. Its activity is tuned by WNK1 phosphorylation of the CID (promoting transcript release and mRNA export), by the cap modification m6Am (which sequesters PCF11 to suppress premature termination), and by condensate formation with unphosphorylated Spt5 facilitated by PP1/PNUTS phosphatase during termination and piRNA-guided silencing [PMID:29196535, PMID:39481383, PMID:40015272].

PDCD2 is a dedicated co-translational chaperone for the 40S ribosomal protein uS5 (RPS2), essential for ribosome biogenesis, stem cell maintenance, and hematopoiesis. PDCD2 binds uS5 co-translationally via a conserved FxxGFG motif in the uS5 N-terminus, escorts uS5 from the cytoplasm to nuclear ribosome assembly sites, and is required for proper 40S subunit synthesis; loss of PDCD2 phenocopies uS5 deficiency and causes rRNA processing defects [PMID:33245768, PMID:41933732, PMID:40208938]. Through its MYND domain, PDCD2 also interacts with HCF-1 and N-CoR/mSin3A corepressor complexes, and its transcription is directly repressed by BCL6 [PMID:12149646, PMID:11854457]. PDCD2 is essential for mouse embryonic development and ESC maintenance, with its loss triggering p53-dependent G1 arrest, and biallelic loss-of-function variants in PDCD2 cause a human ribosomopathy [PMID:20813103, PMID:25150276, PMID:40208938].

PDCD2 is a dedicated co-translational chaperone for the 40S ribosomal protein uS5 (RPS2), essential for ribosome biogenesis, stem cell maintenance, and hematopoiesis. PDCD2 binds uS5 co-translationally via a conserved FxxGFG motif in the uS5 N-terminus, escorts uS5 from the cytoplasm to nuclear ribosome assembly sites, and is required for proper 40S subunit synthesis; loss of PDCD2 phenocopies uS5 deficiency and causes rRNA processing defects [PMID:33245768, PMID:41933732, PMID:40208938]. Through its MYND domain, PDCD2 also interacts with HCF-1 and N-CoR/mSin3A corepressor complexes, and its transcription is directly repressed by BCL6 [PMID:12149646, PMID:11854457]. PDCD2 is essential for mouse embryonic development and ESC maintenance, with its loss triggering p53-dependent G1 arrest, and biallelic loss-of-function variants in PDCD2 cause a human ribosomopathy [PMID:20813103, PMID:25150276, PMID:40208938].

PES1 (Pescadillo) is a nucleolar protein essential for large ribosomal subunit biogenesis and with expanding roles in telomere maintenance, estrogen receptor signaling, and immune evasion. It assembles with Bop1 and WDR12 into the PeBoW complex, which is required for processing of 32S/36S precursor rRNA into mature 28S and 5.8S rRNA; its BRCT domain is indispensable for nucleolar localization, PeBoW incorporation, and rRNA processing function, and disruption of the complex triggers p53 accumulation and cell cycle arrest [PMID:15225545, PMID:16043514, PMID:17189298]. Beyond ribosome biogenesis, PES1 directly interacts with TERT to promote telomerase RNA–TERT assembly and telomerase activity [PMID:31106266], differentially stabilizes ERα while destabilizing ERβ through CHIP-mediated ubiquitination—a process counteracted by SUMO-1/2/3 modification at K517 [PMID:22820289, PMID:27409667]—and suppresses CD8⁺ T cell–mediated immune surveillance by disrupting the ILF3–IL15 mRNA stabilization complex [PMID:36959575]. PES1 protein stability is itself regulated by Trim23-mediated ubiquitination, which is inhibited by the lncRNA SNHG17 [PMID:34782005].
